fruits.extendedStory: On the Burg two churches sit one above the other in the same building. The lower one is the older, Romanesque, from 1157. Romanesque means thick walls, round arches and very little light. It feels like a cave cut out of stone. The upper church took its present shape in 1819 and is bright and full of colour. One staircase carries you from one century into the other.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Am Burg stehen zwei Kirchen übereinander im selben Haus. Die untere ist die ältere, romanisch, aus dem Jahr 1157. Romanisch heißt: dicke Mauern, runde Bögen, wenig Licht. Es fühlt sich an wie eine Höhle aus Stein. Die obere Kirche bekam 1819 ihre heutige Gestalt und ist hell und farbig. Man geht durch eine Treppe aus dem einen Jahrhundert ins andere.
localizedExtendedStory.en: On the Burg two churches sit one above the other in the same building. The lower one is the older, Romanesque, from 1157. Romanesque means thick walls, round arches and very little light. It feels like a cave cut out of stone. The upper church took its present shape in 1819 and is bright and full of colour. One staircase carries you from one century into the other.

localizedStory.de: Zwei Kirchen übereinander am Burgplatz. Die untere ist romanisch und stammt von 1157.
localizedStory.en: Two churches stacked in one building on the Burg. The lower one is Romanesque, from 1157.

fruits.name: Basiliek van het Heilig Bloed
fruits.story: Two churches stacked in one building on the Burg. The lower one is Romanesque, from 1157.

fruits.extendedStory: Work started in 1377 and the building opened in 1421. The city has been governed from it ever since, so for more than six hundred years. The front is Gothic through and through. Tall narrow windows, a turret on every corner, carved stone wherever a flat wall might have gone. In 1852 the whole facade was thoroughly restored.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Die Arbeit begann 1377, und 1421 war das Haus fertig. Seither wird die Stadt von hier aus regiert, also seit über sechshundert Jahren. Die Fassade ist Gotik: hohe schmale Fenster, Türmchen an jeder Ecke, überall Stein statt Fläche. 1852 wurde sie gründlich wiederhergestellt. Wer davorsteht, schaut auf sechs Jahrhunderte Stadtgeschichte an einem Stück.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Work started in 1377 and the building opened in 1421. The city has been governed from it ever since, so for more than six hundred years. The front is Gothic through and through. Tall narrow windows, a turret on every corner, carved stone wherever a flat wall might have gone. In 1852 the whole facade was thoroughly restored.

localizedStory.de: Ein gotisches Rathaus, begonnen 1377 und 1421 eröffnet. Brügge regiert seit über sechshundert Jahren von hier aus.
localizedStory.en: A Gothic town hall, begun in 1377 and opened in 1421. Bruges has been run from here for over six hundred years.

fruits.name: Stadhuis Brugge
fruits.story: A Gothic town hall, begun in 1377 and opened in 1421. Bruges has been run from here for over six hundred years.

fruits.extendedStory: The tower is 122.3 metres high and built entirely of brick. You can pick it out from almost anywhere in the city. Work began in 1210, in the Gothic style, with Karel De Wulf among its builders. The church is named for Mary, in Dutch Onze-Lieve-Vrouw, which means Our Dear Lady. That is where the street beside it gets its name.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Turm ist 122,3 Meter hoch und ganz aus Backstein. Von fast überall in der Stadt sieht man ihn. Gebaut wurde ab 1210, in Gotik, mit Karel De Wulf als einem der Baumeister. Die Kirche ist Maria geweiht, auf Niederländisch Onze-Lieve-Vrouw, unsere liebe Frau. Daher der Name der Straße nebenan.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The tower is 122.3 metres high and built entirely of brick. You can pick it out from almost anywhere in the city. Work began in 1210, in the Gothic style, with Karel De Wulf among its builders. The church is named for Mary, in Dutch Onze-Lieve-Vrouw, which means Our Dear Lady. That is where the street beside it gets its name.

localizedStory.de: Der Backsteinturm misst 122,3 Meter. Über Brügge kommt nichts höher hinaus.
localizedStory.en: The brick tower stands 122.3 metres tall. Nothing in Bruges reaches higher.

fruits.name: Onze-Lieve-Vrouwekerk
fruits.story: The brick tower stands 122.3 metres tall. Nothing in Bruges reaches higher.

fruits.extendedStory: The court was laid out in 1244 for women who lived and worked together without entering a convent. The last beguine moved in in 1925. People still live here even so, a convent community and single women in the small white houses. In 1926 sixty-two poplars and limes were planted across the courtyard, replacing elms that had fallen sick. Under them, every spring, the whole grass comes up in daffodils.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Hof wurde 1244 angelegt, für Frauen, die zusammen lebten und arbeiteten, ohne in ein Kloster einzutreten. Die letzte Begine zog 1925 ein. Gewohnt wird hier trotzdem weiter: heute von einer Klostergemeinschaft und von alleinstehenden Frauen. 1926 wurden 62 Pappeln und Linden im Hof gepflanzt, als Ersatz für erkrankte Ulmen. Unter ihnen steht im Frühjahr die ganze Wiese voller Narzissen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The court was laid out in 1244 for women who lived and worked together without entering a convent. The last beguine moved in in 1925. People still live here even so, a convent community and single women in the small white houses. In 1926 sixty-two poplars and limes were planted across the courtyard, replacing elms that had fallen sick. Under them, every spring, the whole grass comes up in daffodils.

localizedStory.de: Ein stiller Hof von 1244, in dem noch immer gewohnt wird. Im Frühjahr steht die Wiese voller Narzissen.
localizedStory.en: A quiet courtyard from 1244, still lived in. In spring the whole lawn comes up in daffodils.

fruits.name: Begijnhof Ten Wijngaerde
fruits.story: A quiet courtyard from 1244, still lived in. In spring the whole lawn comes up in daffodils.

fruits.extendedStory: In 1200 the count of Flanders handed the lords of Gruuthuse a monopoly. They alone could sell gruut, a mix of bog myrtle and other local herbs. The recipe was often kept secret. The money it brought in shows in the house. In the 1470s Louis of Gruuthuse had a private oratory built. From it he and his wife followed the services next door in the Church of Our Lady. The palace has been a museum since 1876.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Graf von Flandern gab den Herren von Gruuthuse im Jahr 1200 ein Monopol. Sie allein durften Gruut verkaufen, eine Mischung aus Gagel und anderen heimischen Kräutern. Das Rezept blieb oft geheim. Reich geworden, ließ Ludwig von Gruuthuse sich in den 1470er Jahren ein privates Oratorium bauen. Von dort aus verfolgten er und seine Frau die Messen nebenan in der Liebfrauenkirche. Seit 1876 ist der Palast ein Museum.
localizedExtendedStory.en: In 1200 the count of Flanders handed the lords of Gruuthuse a monopoly. They alone could sell gruut, a mix of bog myrtle and other local herbs. The recipe was often kept secret. The money it brought in shows in the house. In the 1470s Louis of Gruuthuse had a private oratory built. From it he and his wife followed the services next door in the Church of Our Lady. The palace has been a museum since 1876.

localizedStory.de: Diese Familie besaß ab 1200 das Gruutrecht: das alleinige Recht, eine geheime Kräutermischung zu verkaufen.
localizedStory.en: This family held the gruut right from 1200. Nobody else was allowed to sell a certain secret mix of herbs.

fruits.name: Gruuthusemuseum
fruits.story: This family held the gruut right from 1200. Nobody else was allowed to sell a certain secret mix of herbs.

fruits.extendedStory: This tower was once the safest place in town. The city charters, the city seal and the town funds were kept up here. They sat in iron boxes with padlocks, in niches behind double wrought-iron doors. Between 1482 and 1486 an eight-sided sandstone stage was added on top. Forty-seven bells hang inside today, 26 of them the original 18th-century ones. Anyone who wants to hear them close up takes the 366 steps.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Turm war einmal der sicherste Ort der Stadt. Hier oben lagen die Stadturkunden, das Stadtsiegel und die Stadtkasse. Sie steckten in Eisenkisten mit Vorhängeschlössern, in Nischen hinter doppelten schmiedeeisernen Türen. Zwischen 1482 und 1486 setzte man dem Turm noch einen achteckigen Sandsteinaufsatz auf. Heute hängen 47 Glocken darin, 26 davon die originalen aus dem 18. Jahrhundert. Wer sie aus der Nähe hören will, nimmt die 366 Stufen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: This tower was once the safest place in town. The city charters, the city seal and the town funds were kept up here. They sat in iron boxes with padlocks, in niches behind double wrought-iron doors. Between 1482 and 1486 an eight-sided sandstone stage was added on top. Forty-seven bells hang inside today, 26 of them the original 18th-century ones. Anyone who wants to hear them close up takes the 366 steps.

localizedStory.de: 83 Meter hoch, und 366 Stufen führen hinauf. Ganz oben hängen 47 Glocken.
localizedStory.en: 83 metres tall, and 366 steps lead to the top. Forty-seven bells hang up there.

fruits.name: Belfort
fruits.story: 83 metres tall, and 366 steps lead to the top. Forty-seven bells hang up there.

fruits.extendedStory: In 1294 the Augustinian friars were allowed to throw a bridge across the water straight in front of their friary. The one standing there now was built in 1391 by the Bruges master mason Jan van Oudenaerde. The best part of it shows once you are on it. Stone benches are built into the inside of the parapets. You can sit down out in the middle and watch the boats go under.

localizedExtendedStory.de: 1294 durften die Augustiner direkt vor ihrem Kloster eine Brücke über das Wasser schlagen. Die Brücke, die heute dort steht, baute 1391 der Brügger Baumeister Jan van Oudenaerde. Das Schöne daran sieht man erst, wenn man daraufsteht. In die Innenseiten der Brüstungen sind Steinbänke eingebaut. Man kann sich hinsetzen, mitten über dem Wasser, und den Booten zusehen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: In 1294 the Augustinian friars were allowed to throw a bridge across the water straight in front of their friary. The one standing there now was built in 1391 by the Bruges master mason Jan van Oudenaerde. The best part of it shows once you are on it. Stone benches are built into the inside of the parapets. You can sit down out in the middle and watch the boats go under.

localizedStory.de: In die Brüstungen dieser Brücke sind Steinbänke eingebaut. Man kann sich also mitten aufs Wasser setzen.
localizedStory.en: Stone benches are built into this bridge's parapets. You can sit down right over the water.

fruits.name: Augustijnenbrug
fruits.story: Stone benches are built into this bridge's parapets. You can sit down right over the water.

fruits.extendedStory: Officially this little square has no name at all. On paper it counts as part of Katelijnestraat. Everyone in Bruges calls it the Ankerplaats regardless. The name comes from an inn called L'Ancre, the anchor, which goes back at least to the 16th century. A written mention of it turns up in 1579. The city's diamond museum stands on this square that is not a square.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Offiziell hat dieser kleine Platz gar keinen Namen. Auf dem Papier gehört er zur Katelijnestraat. Die Brügger nennen ihn trotzdem alle Ankerplaats. Der Name kommt von einem Gasthaus namens L'Ancre, dem Anker, das mindestens bis ins 16. Jahrhundert zurückreicht. 1579 taucht es in einer Aufzeichnung auf. Heute liegt das Brügger Diamantmuseum an diesem Platz, den es offiziell nicht gibt.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Officially this little square has no name at all. On paper it counts as part of Katelijnestraat. Everyone in Bruges calls it the Ankerplaats regardless. The name comes from an inn called L'Ancre, the anchor, which goes back at least to the 16th century. A written mention of it turns up in 1579. The city's diamond museum stands on this square that is not a square.

localizedStory.de: Ein Platz, den es offiziell gar nicht gibt. Die Brügger nennen ihn trotzdem seit Jahrhunderten so.
localizedStory.en: A square that officially does not exist. People in Bruges have called it this for centuries anyway.

fruits.name: Ankerplein
fruits.story: A square that officially does not exist. People in Bruges have called it this for centuries anyway.

fruits.extendedStory: It turns up in writing as a parish church in 1086, and building work began in 1275. The cathedral title came much later, in 1834. The Bruges diocese was being re-founded, and the cathedral it had belonged to, Sint-Donaas, had already been demolished in 1799. So this church stepped up. A fire took the roofs and the top of the tower in 1839. The English architect R. Chantrell drew the replacement, built between 1843 and 1846.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Als Pfarrkirche taucht sie 1086 erstmals in den Schriften auf, gebaut wurde ab 1275. Den Titel Kathedrale erbte sie erst 1834. Das Bistum Brügge wurde damals neu gegründet, und die bisherige Kathedrale Sint-Donaas war schon 1799 abgerissen worden. Also rückte diese Kirche nach. 1839 nahm ein Feuer die Dächer und die Turmspitze. Den Ersatz zeichnete der englische Architekt R. Chantrell, gebaut 1843 bis 1846.
localizedExtendedStory.en: It turns up in writing as a parish church in 1086, and building work began in 1275. The cathedral title came much later, in 1834. The Bruges diocese was being re-founded, and the cathedral it had belonged to, Sint-Donaas, had already been demolished in 1799. So this church stepped up. A fire took the roofs and the top of the tower in 1839. The English architect R. Chantrell drew the replacement, built between 1843 and 1846.

localizedStory.de: Kathedrale wurde sie 1834, als die eigentliche Kathedrale der Stadt längst abgerissen war.
localizedStory.en: It became a cathedral in 1834, long after the city's actual cathedral had been pulled down.

fruits.name: Sint-Salvatorskathedraal
fruits.story: It became a cathedral in 1834, long after the city's actual cathedral had been pulled down.
